lines: Tabletop RPGs are the best games you've never played.
No screen, no controller. Just you, some friends, or soon-to-be friends, a pile of dice, and a story no one's told before.
Here is where we'll get you started.

howToSteps.heading: Find your system
howToSteps.body: Not sure what to play? Take the quiz below. Already know? Skip ahead to the cards.

howToSteps.heading: Get the free rules
howToSteps.body: Most systems have free starter rules. All links labelled. You'll know before you click whether it's free, needs registration, or costs money.

howToSteps.heading: Know what you need
howToSteps.body: At minimum: the rules, a character sheet, and somewhere to play (a VTT if online). Most of this is free.

howToSteps.heading: Find your group
howToSteps.body: Discord servers with active LFG channels below. How to write an LFG post that actually gets accepted. Both are below.

howToSteps.heading: Find a GM and start playing
howToSteps.body: Links to Discord LFG servers. Roll20 free account lets you play in the browser tonight.

links.label: StartPlaying.games: skip the queue, get a professional GM this week

howToSteps.heading: AI options exist
howToSteps.body: Not the same as playing with real people. No banter, no shared memory, no chaos. But if you need to roll dice this second, they're out there.

terminology.definition: Player Character. That's you. The person you play in the game world.
Non-Player Character. Everyone else. The bartender, the crime boss, the dragon. The GM plays all of them.

Game Master. Also called Dungeon Master in D&D, Storyteller in Vampire, Keeper in Call of Cthulhu. This person builds and runs the world for everyone else. They fill in all the blanks so you can enjoy the story without building it. You might want to become one someday. Right now you're probably just looking for one.
Every system has its own name for this. It's how your character grows and gets better. D&D calls it Experience Points. Shadowrun calls it Karma. Some systems skip it entirely.
One sitting of play. Usually two to four hours. A campaign is many sessions. A one-shot is a complete story in one session.
The meeting before the campaign starts. No dice. Everyone agrees on the kind of story they want, what's off limits, and who their characters are.
Virtual Tabletop. Software your group uses to play online. Roll20, Foundry, Owlbear Rodeo. You'll need an account before most online groups accept you.
A complete game in a single session. No commitment. Great for beginners.

Looking For Group. What you post when you want to find players or a GM. You'll see LFG channels in most TTRPG Discord servers. A good LFG post is specific: system, timezone, availability, experience level.

systems.name: D&D 5e
systems.tagline: The one everyone's heard of. Be an edgy rogue, a righteous paladin, a monster-slaying barbarian. Fight things. Loot dungeons. Laugh it off in a tavern.
systems.socialProof: As seen on Critical Role and Dimension 20. Free rules on D&D Beyond. No purchase required to start.
systems.willIDie: Rarely. D&D is forgiving by default.
systems.quizResultWhy: Your answers describe a classic heroic adventure. D&D has the biggest community, the most resources, and a free ruleset you can open right now. Start here.

systems.name: Vampire: The Masquerade
systems.tagline: You're dead. You've been dead for three hundred years. Now you run the city, or you're trying to. Politics, betrayal, and the monster you're slowly becoming.
systems.socialProof: If you've ever watched anything gothic and thought "I want to be that"? This is your game.
systems.easyToLearn: Medium. The rules serve the story, not the other way around.
systems.willIDie: Yes, and it'll mean something when it happens
systems.campaignLength: Medium to long. Political intrigue needs time to breathe.
systems.quizResultWhy: You want politics, power, and a character who wrestles with what they're becoming. Vampire puts all of that at the centre of every session.
systems.edition_note: V5 is current. V20 is still widely played. Vampire: The Requiem is a separate game. Different lore, different clans, different world. Check which edition your group is running before buying.

systems.name: Shadowrun 5e
systems.tagline: Corporate dystopia. Cybernetic implants. Magic came back and nobody asked for it. You're a criminal for hire in a world that would rather you didn't exist. Run fast. Shoot straight. Never deal with a dragon.
systems.socialProof: If Cyberpunk and fantasy had a baby and that baby had a shotgun.
systems.easyToLearn: Hard, but worth it. The crunch is part of the flavour.
systems.willIDie: Frequently. This world is not on your side.
systems.campaignLength: Flexible. Single runs or full campaigns.
systems.quizResultWhy: Crew dynamics, corporate warfare, and a world that wants you dead. Shadowrun rewards players who plan and improvise in equal measure.

systems.name: Shadowrun Anarchy
systems.tagline: Same world as Shadowrun. Same neon-drenched corporate nightmare. Half the rulebook. There's no GM. Players share the storytelling between them. If you want the flavour without the spreadsheet, start here.
systems.willIDie: Yes. The world is still hostile, the rules are just kinder.
systems.campaignLength: Short to medium. Fast and loose by design.
systems.quizResultWhy: Same world as Shadowrun, half the rulebook. Anarchy gets you into the cyberpunk fiction fast without the character-building spreadsheet.

systems.name: Call of Cthulhu
systems.tagline: You're not the hero. You're an accountant from Ohio who just found something in the library that cannot be unread. You will investigate. You will probably regret it.
systems.socialProof: Cthulhu is everywhere: the memes, the plushies, the references. The game is better than all of them.
systems.easyToLearn: Yes, one of the simplest systems on this list
systems.willIDie: Yes. Or worse, go mad. Probably both.
systems.campaignLength: Short to medium. Most scenarios are self-contained.

freeRules.label: Free quickstart including The Haunting adventure

systems.quizResultWhy: You want mystery, dread, and the creeping certainty that you are not equipped for what you found. Call of Cthulhu delivers this in one of the most accessible systems on this list.

systems.name: Pathfinder 2e
systems.tagline: D&D's more tactical sibling. Every choice matters, every build is deliberate, every combat is a puzzle. If you've outgrown 5e and want more depth. This is where you go next.
systems.socialProof: Full free rules at Archives of Nethys. No purchase required, ever.
systems.easyToLearn: Medium to hard. More options than D&D, well documented.
systems.willIDie: Sometimes. More dangerous than D&D, less brutal than OSR systems.
systems.quizResultWhy: You want tactical depth and options that reward careful play. Pathfinder 2e has one of the most complete rulesets available, and the whole thing is free.

systems.name: FATE Core
systems.tagline: No setting. No genre. No limits. FATE is a storytelling engine. You bring the world, it handles the rest. If you've got a concept that doesn't fit anything else, it fits here.
systems.socialProof: Completely free. Pay what you want directly from the publisher.
systems.easyToLearn: Medium. Simple rules, but thinking in aspects takes adjustment.
systems.willIDie: Rarely. FATE is built for protagonists, not casualties.
systems.quizResultWhy: Your concept doesn't fit neatly into any other box. FATE is a storytelling engine that works for any genre and hands narrative control to the table.

systems.name: Mothership
systems.tagline: Deep space. No heroes. Your ship's life support is failing, something got into the cargo hold, and the corporation doesn't care if you make it back. Survive if you can.
systems.socialProof: Indie darling of the OSR scene. The best sci-fi horror RPG running right now.
systems.campaignLength: Short. Horror works best in concentrated doses.
systems.quizResultWhy: Survival horror in deep space with stripped-back rules and no pretense that you're the hero. Mothership does one thing and does it better than anything else.

systems.name: Mörk Borg
systems.tagline: The world is ending. It has been ending for a while. You are not special. Go find something worth dying for.
systems.socialProof: Won every indie RPG award going. Also looks incredible on a table.
systems.campaignLength: Short. Characters rarely survive long enough for campaigns.
systems.quizResultWhy: Short, brutal, and unlike anything else. Mörk Borg is a one-session death spiral with artwork that looks like a metal album cover. It earns every award it has won.

systems.name: Cairn
systems.tagline: Dark forests. Ancient ruins. No classes, no levels, just what you carry and how clever you are. Old school survival fantasy stripped to its bones.
systems.socialProof: Free. Completely free. Always will be.
systems.easyToLearn: Yes, one of the fastest to learn on this list
systems.willIDie: Yes. The forest doesn't care about your backstory.
systems.quizResultWhy: Old-school survival fantasy with no filler. Cairn is completely free, one of the fastest to learn on this list, and trusts you to play smart.

systems.name: Legend of the Five Rings
systems.tagline: Feudal Japan. Samurai, courtiers, and monks in a world where honour is currency and a single wrong word ends your life faster than any blade.
systems.socialProof: A dice system unlike anything else at the table. Rolling and reading them is half the experience.
systems.easyToLearn: Medium to hard. The dice pool takes an hour to get comfortable with, and you'll want to know the factions before session one
systems.willIDie: Yes, and honour demands you face it with dignity
systems.campaignLength: Medium to long. The political web needs time to tangle.
dice: Custom d10 ring and skill dice
systems.quizResultWhy: Political drama, honour as a game mechanic, and a world where one wrong word ends you faster than any blade. Legend of the Five Rings is unlike anything else on this list.

quiz.title: What tabletop RPG should you play?
quiz.subtitle: Eight questions. Honest answers. One recommendation, plus your runner-up.
quiz.sharePreText: Not sure what RPG to play? Take this quiz and find your system. Share it with your group so everyone finds theirs.

questions.text: When you imagine your ideal story, what's the setting?

options.text: Swords, magic, dragons. Classic high fantasy.
Dark city streets, rain on neon, corporate dystopia, cybernetic augmentation, guns and vehicles
Gothic horror: old mansions, political intrigue, things that go bump
Deep space, alien worlds, the unknown frontier
Gritty survival: post-apocalypse, no heroes, just people trying to live
Feudal honour: samurai, courtiers, a world where one wrong word ends you

questions.text: When you sit down at the table, what do you actually want to do?

options.text: Fight: tactical combat, knowing my build cold
Talk: negotiate, manipulate, charm, deceive
Investigate: uncover mysteries and secrets
Become someone: deep character, personal story arc
Build and acquire: resources, territory, power
Cause chaos: unpredictable, impulsive, consequences be damned
All of this sounds good

questions.text: How do you feel about rules and mechanics?

options.text: I want deep mechanics. I like knowing exactly how everything works.
I want enough rules to feel fair but I don't want homework
Get out of my way. I want to roleplay, not do maths.
I've never played before. I need something that teaches me as I go.

questions.text: Who do you want to be at the table?

options.text: A hero, maybe flawed, but fundamentally trying to do good
A survivor: morality is a luxury, staying alive isn't
A monster: powerful, dangerous, wrestling with what that means
An operator: professional, skilled, the job comes first
A wildcard. I genuinely don't know what my character will do next.
The joker: comic relief, chaos merchant, the one who makes the table laugh
A builder: networks, influence, power, politics. I want to own the throne, or build a better world trying.

questions.text: When things go wrong, and they will, how does your character handle it?

options.text: Fight through it: aggression, power, direct confrontation
Talk your way out: lies, charm, negotiation
Disappear: disengage, regroup, come back smarter
Sacrifice something: relationships, morality, resources
Adapt and improvise. No plan survives contact with the enemy.
Rally others: my strength is in who I know and who trusts me

questions.text: What kind of story do you actually want to tell?

options.text: Me against the world: personal struggle, internal demons, who am I becoming
Us against the world: crew dynamics, loyalty, pulling off the impossible together
Uncovering the truth: conspiracies, mysteries, nothing is what it seems
Climbing the ladder: reputation, power, becoming untouchable
Surviving the world: it's hostile, it's brutal, just getting through is enough
Changing the world: my character will leave a mark, for better or worse

questions.text: Let's talk about dice. How do you feel about them?

options.text: Give me ALL of them: d4 d6 d8 d10 d12 d20, the weird ones, the pretty ones. I want a bag that rattles.
I need dice at the table: rolling a handful and counting successes is half the fun
One type of die is fine: keep it simple, same die every time
Dice are fine but I could take or leave them
Please don't make me do dice maths

questions.text: One last thing. How do you feel about conflict with other players?

options.text: Love it: I want to scheme against, betray, and outmanoeuvre the people I'm sitting with
Occasionally fine. If it emerges naturally from the story, great.
I'd rather not. We're a team working against the world.
Hard no. If my character gets stabbed in the back by another player, I'm going home.

aiGameMasters.name: Questwright
aiGameMasters.pricingNote: Currently in private beta. Free while in beta. Usage-based pricing at launch. Beta testers get favourable terms.
aiGameMasters.description: Purpose-built TTRPG platform. Persistent character sheets, real dice mechanics, proper game state tracking, procedural world generation, tactical battle maps, NPC memory, and a rules engine that enforces actual game rules. D&D 5e and Pathfinder supported. Solo or multiplayer. The closest thing to a real TTRPG with an AI GM that currently exists.

aiGameMasters.name: Friends and Fables
aiGameMasters.pricingNote: Free tier: 5–25 AI turns per day. Paid plans from $19.95/month for unlimited turns and more players.
aiGameMasters.description: AI GM called Franz. Tracks character sheets, inventory, locations, and health automatically. D&D 5e mechanics. Built for both veterans with scheduling problems and complete newcomers.

aiGameMasters.name: LoreKeeper
aiGameMasters.pricingNote: Free tier: 20 turns per day, no card required. Paid tiers unlock more. The host's plan covers a session. Guests don't need their own subscription.
aiGameMasters.description: AI GM with persistent campaigns and multiplayer up to six players.

aiGameMasters.name: MasterAI
aiGameMasters.pricingNote: Free to play. Earns in-app tokens through play.
aiGameMasters.description: Mobile app. 12 classes, 8 races, levels 1 to 20, automatic character progression, 3D dice.

gameMasterSection.heading: Thinking about running your own game?
gameMasterSection.body: Running a game is different from playing one. You're building the world, playing every NPC, and keeping five people engaged at once. It's the best seat at the table. The /start page has what you need to get your friends through the door.
